post.summary: An admin (CLEARANCE_ADMINS), or a delegate naming one in the on-behalf-of header, opens a break-glass window on one protected environment: a reason, a TTL (a Go duration, at most CLEARANCE_BREAKGLASS_MAX_TTL, never over 4h) and the cluster and env. Recorded as breakglass.open and committed before the answer, so the record precedes every change it covers. It clears nothing; exceptions inside it carry its id. At the TTL the core reconciles it (breakglass.close). The call may carry X-Clearance-Via (cli, web, slack, api, or a name from CLEARANCE_VIAS_EXTRA) and X-Clearance-Surface-Ref (at most 512 bytes of printable text), recorded as claimed `surface` {via, ref}; a bad value is 400 (DG-VIA, DG-SURFACE-REF). A delegate naming the person may forward their sign-in time in X-Clearance-Auth-Time (unix seconds), which CLEARANCE_FRESH_AUTH_DELEGATES=require demands.

put.summary: The provider's whole set of cluster-pinned agent definitions (its Agent XR loader's pins and rejections) replaces the set the core holds. The core decides each pin itself (schema, name, owner, workload identity, not a bundled name) and records each change once as definition.load, definition.unload or definition.reject; provenance then reads the pinned definitions. The optional bundled list is the definitions that ship with the provider itself (name, build version, document): decided with the same schema, held beside the pins (a pin cannot shadow one) and recorded the same way; absent keeps the provider's earlier bundled set. Only the provider registered with definitions: true.

post.summary: Bulk resolution: a person (an admin, CLEARANCE_ADMINS, or a delegate naming one in the on-behalf-of header) resolves up to 200 observations or gate exceptions at once with the same state, cause and note as POST /v1/observations/{seq}/resolution. Each item gets a resolution record of its own, exactly as the single route writes it (about that seq, naming the person), never one record for many; every record of the call carries the same resolution.batch {id, size}. The records are written in one transaction. The answer names the batch and, for each item, the record written (recorded), why it was skipped (skipped: not an observation or a resolvable exception, a seq named twice, or its newest resolution already has the same state, cause and note) or why its record was refused (failed). The same validation as the single route: a state or cause outside the vocabulary, or reverted without a cause, refuses the whole call with 400. The call may carry X-Clearance-Via (cli, web, slack, api, or a name from CLEARANCE_VIAS_EXTRA) and X-Clearance-Surface-Ref (at most 512 bytes of printable text), recorded as claimed `surface` {via, ref}; a bad value is 400 (DG-VIA, DG-SURFACE-REF). A delegate naming the person may forward their sign-in time in X-Clearance-Auth-Time (unix seconds), which CLEARANCE_FRESH_AUTH_DELEGATES=require demands.

post.summary: A person (an admin, CLEARANCE_ADMINS, or a delegate naming one in the on-behalf-of header) sets how an observed change ended: state (reverted, ratified, declared-break-glass, still-live) and, for reverted, its cause (agent-caused, policy-triggered, human-initiated, automated-remediation, requirement-changed, external-dependency, unattributed), with an optional note. Recorded as a resolution record about the observation, naming the person (principal, initiator, resolution.by). Append-only: an edit is another record about the same seq, and the newest wins when it is read; the earlier ones stay in the chain. The seq may also be a gate exception (deploy.exception of kind out-of-band, drift, untraced-apply or digest-mismatch), resolved in the scope of its destination (cluster, else workspace backend/key#name); attempted-refused and monitoring-protection exceptions are not resolved this way. The call may carry X-Clearance-Via (cli, web, slack, api, or a name from CLEARANCE_VIAS_EXTRA) and X-Clearance-Surface-Ref (at most 512 bytes of printable text), recorded as claimed `surface` {via, ref}; a bad value is 400 (DG-VIA, DG-SURFACE-REF). A delegate naming the person may forward their sign-in time in X-Clearance-Auth-Time (unix seconds), which CLEARANCE_FRESH_AUTH_DELEGATES=require demands.

post.summary: An admin (CLEARANCE_ADMINS, or a delegate naming one) publishes an evidence packet the packet job wrote, as a bundle (the packet directory as one JSON document). The core checks every file against the manifest, that the packet was read from this chain (its head is the hash the core holds at that count), and keeps it. The packet's id is the content's address (pk- and the first 32 hex digits of the SHA-256 of MANIFEST.json): the same packet again is the same id and records nothing; a new one is one packet.publish record.

get.summary: The recipient reads the packet (the bundle) under the credential its delivery returned, in the bearer header. No Clearance account. The credential is checked for its signature (anything the core did not sign is a bare 401); then every answer is a packet.fetch record, written before the answer: an allowed read before a byte is served, and a refusal (PK-EXPIRED, PK-NOT-YET, PK-SCOPE for another packet or a part outside its scope, PK-RECIPIENT, PK-GONE) with its rule.

put.summary: The targets one source (a cluster's gitops render, an account's bootstrap) declares: the Map's registry of what should be protected. Each target has an id, name, kind, group, environment, app, owner, registry tier, the coverage scope its observations arrive under, the gates that guard it (type, instance, mode enforce or flag) and the observers that watch it. The list replaces the set the core holds for that source (an empty list withdraws it); other sources' are untouched. Validated strictly; a changed set is one targets.load record carrying the set's digest, an unchanged one records nothing. Only a provider registered with targets naming the source. clearance-api serves the union (GET /v1/targets).
